answer: A proof-of-useful-work protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve verifiable scientific problems, such as tracking a comet, modeling an optical lantern, or classifying calls of a raven, to register. An attacker must expend scarce computational cycles and electricity on heavy matrix operations per spawned identity rather than virtualizing free nodes. However, verifying these non-trivial solutions requires redundant network computation, creating scalability bottlenecks.
